content: The dosing of aloe varies depending on the specific indication. For oral use, the recommended dosage ranges from 50 to 200 mg per day, or 30 mL taken three times daily. Alternatively, 15 to 60 drops may be taken orally as needed. For topical application, a 1:10 solution with 50% alcohol can be applied three to five times daily as needed. Aloe is commonly used to promote wound healing and is also utilized for its anesthetic, antiseptic, and anti-inflammatory properties. It has been applied in the management of arthritis, burns, cold sores, fever, inflammation, as a moisturizer, and for pruritus. Aloe is considered possibly effective for alleviating pain, reducing inflammation, and promoting wound healing. However, it may cause hypoglycemia in some cases. No significant drug interactions have been reported. Oral use of aloe is contraindicated in individuals with conditions such as abdominal discomfort, appendicitis, Crohn's disease, diabetes mellitus, hemorrhoids, intestinal obstruction, kidney disease, nausea or vomiting, peptic ulcer disease (PUD), and ulcerative colitis. Regarding pregnancy and lactation, aloe has not been assigned a specific pregnancy category. However, it is generally considered acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have not demonstrated evidence of fetal risk.
